column1: # tools/core/int64-allow.tsv -- the sources that keep `# spinel: int64` on a
# 32-bit target.
# On a target whose pointers are 32 bits, the kernel (spinel-core-kernel)
# and spinel-fs-emit refuse a first-line
# `# spinel: int64` unless this table lists the source. A listed source builds
# at 64 bits as before. A source is listed when its bytes are a listed file's
# current bytes, so a lane that compiles a copy is still listed and an edited
# copy is not. `--int64-allow FILE` reads another table; a table's paths are
# relative to the directory two levels above its own (tools/core/ -> the
# repository).
# Every read checks the whole table: a row that is not a path and a reason, a
# path listed twice, a path that does not exist, or a listed file that does
# not declare `# spinel: int64` refuses every source (`int64-allow-table`).
# A row is a deliberate exception: a source whose 64-bit Integer does not matter for
# performance, typically a test whose subject is 64-bit arithmetic or a 64-bit
# platform value, and only where rewriting it at 32 bits would lose what it
# tests.
# COLUMNS
#   path    the source, from the repository root
#   reason  why its 64 bits stay, and why a rewrite would lose the test
#path
